level_domain.field: creature instance byte +0x403 ('Experience level' per the older creature-record notes; the same object type is addressed in both candidate functions)

located_writers.effect: level-up: AL = byte[+0x403]; INC AL; byte[+0x403] = AL
level-down: AL = byte[+0x403]; DEC AL; byte[+0x403] = AL

level_up_cap.derivation: entry check CMP byte[+0x403],0x0a: if level == 10 the function returns without a write; otherwise it writes AL = level+1, so a write can only produce 2..10 from a 1..9 predecessor

level_down_floor.derivation: entry check CMP byte[+0x403],0x1: if level == 1 the function returns without a write; otherwise it writes AL = level-1, so a write can only produce 0..9 from a 1..10 predecessor; combined with init=1 the reachable floor is 1

level_domain.caveat: The domain 1..10 is an inductive invariant over the three writers located by the saved decompile corpus (init=1, +1 capped at 10, -1 floored at 1). It is NOT a proof that no other writer exists (for example a bulk copy/load path); writer enumeration completeness is not established here.
